v0.4.2-candidate-a.decision: Rejected: ranking additional PSM13 output by OCR confidence regressed geography 20/24 to 19/24 and independent math 29/34 to 28/34. Retry only as row-scoped alternatives requiring exact body corroboration.

blind_protocol: Flatland and BERT source hashes and manually annotated body references were fixed before their first recognition run under candidate A; its exact hashes and failures are preserved in prior_independent_evaluations[v0.4.2-first-pass]. A was rejected for regressions on established geography/math, not for these hold-outs. Final runtime C was frozen before revalidation. No rules were fitted to the new hold-out failures. The previous v0.4.1 hold-outs are now regression data. Flatland retains its historical invisible OCR text and is processed with force_ocr on all 116 pages; it has a printed contents list without usable folios. BERT is a 16-page two-column paper without printed contents. These tests expose failure cases, not universal accuracy.

maintenance_comparison.metric_policy: Strict title/PDF-page/depth matching uses existing normalization. Complete-outline samples score every candidate. Chapter/section-only references are partial scopes and do not establish full-output precision. Cache timings are the original raw extraction, not a speed comparison. All final outputs are regenerated and full-page verified under final runtime C; raw extraction caches are reused only when extraction fingerprint is unchanged. Final C changes only heading-stage confirmation relative to B, so raw extraction cache reuse is legitimate.

performance.method: Linux fresh processes, same pinned dependencies/models, 200 DPI. AB then BA after book benchmarks complete. Text measures native extraction plus outline; TOC measures image OCR/layout for the same two 100-DPI/JPEG-30 contents pages. Mean row confidence is a heuristic, not calibrated accuracy. Memory is separate kernel ru_maxrss parent and largest child, not aggregate simultaneous RSS.
performance.driver:
import sys,time,json,resource,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
if __name__=='__main__':
    scripts,mode=sys.argv[1:];sys.path.insert(0,scripts)
    hashes={p.name:hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()for p in Path(scripts).glob("*.py")}
    import add_bookmarks as a
    start=time.perf_counter()
    if mode=='toc':
        rows=[a._read_image_page(('validation/zh-low.pdf',i,'chi_sim+eng','/usr/bin/tesseract',False,200))for i in [3,4]]
        value=dict(primary_rows=sum(line.startswith('[TOC]\t')for _,text,_ in rows for line in text.splitlines()),alternative_rows=sum(line.startswith('[TOC_ALT]\t')for _,text,_ in rows for line in text.splitlines()))
    else:
        pages,scanned,visual=a.read_pages('validation/text.pdf',lang='eng',workers=4,dpi=200)
        value=dict(bookmarks=len(a.headings_from_pages(pages,scanned,visual=visual)),ocr_pages=len(scanned))
    print(json.dumps(dict(version=a.VERSION,implementation_sha256=hashes,mode=mode,seconds=time.perf_counter()-start,parent_peak_rss_mib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss/1024,largest_child_peak_rss_mib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss/1024,**value)))
performance.interpretation: Two repetitions only. Extra OCR alternatives cost time on the two low-quality TOC pages. No general speed or memory improvement is claimed; no resolution, OCR languages, tests or platforms were removed.

maintenance_comparison.ci_policy: Three platforms by Python 3.10-3.13, mandatory OCR, zero skipped tests. 108 local tests. Current remote job timings and results must be inspected after push, not fabricated in this pre-push report.

failure_analysis.finding: 17/32 instead of 16/32. One alternative is corroborated by exact body wording at the confirmed destination, with matching numeric marker even when body OCR omits that marker. Remaining substitutions, missing rows and page/level errors remain unresolved; no book-specific correction dictionary or reference-driven output repair.

failure_analysis.scope: Complete printed contents including units and appendices; every generated bookmark is scored, including duplicates and extra titles. Extra body headings are not necessarily invalid navigation, but are outside this predefined contents policy.
failure_analysis.finding: 20/24 retained. OCR confidence ranking alone caused a regression in rejected A. Extra fallback remains an alternative and cannot replace a primary without exact target-body corroboration.

failure_analysis.scope: All 24 body part/section headers, wording and destinations checked from page images; printed contents omits folios and differs from some body titles. Existing invisible OCR layer retained unchanged but image OCR is forced for this benchmark.
failure_analysis.finding: Default force-OCR output matches only 1/24 body outline references, with running headers and dialogue misread as headings. Printed contents have no usable folios, and italic section headings/markers are missed. This is an observed limitation, not a passed recognition test.

failure_analysis.scope: All 29 numbered body/appendix headings in the two-column paper. No printed contents. Unnumbered abstract, references and appendix banner are outside this explicit policy; every output candidate is scored.
failure_analysis.finding: Default finds no headings: small numbered bold headings are below default visual-size filtering and multiline/two-column structure is incomplete. Extended mode finds some titles but still misses wrapped headings and parent structure. No headings means no automatic PDF; manual source-reviewed import is validated separately.

warnings: OCR headings are unverified; review titles, hierarchy and page destinations with --analyze before use.
